* [[Ali Abdullah Saleh]], in office since 1978, is [[Yemen presidential election, 2006|re-elected]] as [[List of Presidents of Yemen|President]] of [[Yemen]] with 77.2% of the votes, prompting allegations of [[electoral fraud]] from the [[Faisal Bin Shamlan|Yemeni opposition coalition]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/5374606.stm (BBC)]
* In an interview with ''[[Fox News Sunday]]'', to be aired on [[September 24]], [[President of the United States|Former U.S. President]] [[Bill Clinton]] says, "At least I tried. That's the difference in me and some, including all of the right-wingers who are attacking me now," responding to those who criticize him for the [[September 11th terrorist attacks]], "They had eight months to try, they did not try. I tried. So I tried and failed." [http://reuters.myway.com/article/20060923/2006-09-23T034256Z_01_N22174760_RTRIDST_0_NEWS-SECURITY-CLINTON-DC.html (Reuters)]
* [[Toomas Hendrik Ilves]] is elected the new [[President of Estonia]], defeating incumbent [[Arnold Rüütel]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/5373874.stm (BBC)]
* [[France|French]] authorities are investigating reports that [[Osama bin Laden]] has died of [[typhoid]] after a leaked French secret service report. [[Time (magazine)|''Time'' magazine]] also cites an unknown [[Saudi Arabia]]n source that Bin Laden had a waterborne disease and may be dead. However, French and U.S. authorities are unable to confirm these reports. [http://www.ctv.ca/servlet/ArticleNews/story/CTVNews/20060923/binladen_report_060923/20060923?hub=TopStories (CTV NEWS)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061004004558/http://www.ctv.ca/servlet/ArticleNews/story/CTVNews/20060923/binladen_report_060923/20060923?hub=TopStories |date=2006-10-04 }} [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/5374160.stm (BBC News)] [https://web.archive.org/web/20070331061726/http://today.reuters.com/news/articlenews.aspx?type=worldNews (Reuters)]

* Japan's [[Hinode (satellite)|Solar-B]] mission is launched from the [[Uchinoura Space Center]].  With its successful launch, it is rechristened "Hinode". [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sci/tech/5371162.stm (BBC)]
